downloads.dek: By sector, source category and greenhouse gas, with the evidence grade on every row.
downloads.title: Annual emissions

downloads.dek: Annual estimates for each province. Emissions are not measured provincially, so these are allocations — but the road-fuel split rides OCAC's own provincial sales, not a proxy.

downloads.dek: Every month of the record, saying for each whether the timing is observed, modelled or evenly spread.

collections.title: Emissions estimates

downloads.dek: Petrol, diesel, furnace oil, kerosene and aviation fuel as OCAC publishes them, by customer class. Sales into a class, not fuel burned in it.

downloads.dek: The same publication's monthly area pages, province by province. Fuel sold in a province is not fuel burned there — freight crosses boundaries.
downloads.title: Petroleum sales by area

downloads.dek: Census counts by animal type, province and district, with the Economic Survey's forward estimate labelled a projection and never summed with them.

downloads.dek: Area and production by crop, year and district. A district figure split from a pooled parent is marked an allocation, not an observation.

downloads.dek: Monthly product offtake and nutrient totals. Offtake is distribution, not application to fields, and tonnes of product are never tonnes of nitrogen.

downloads.dek: Plant-level fuel quantity and net generation from the regulator's own tables, with the implied heat rate marked as derived.

downloads.dek: Electricity generated, plant by plant, month by month. Generation only — the fuel behind it was never measured monthly.
downloads.title: Monthly plant generation

downloads.dek: Design-weighted survey aggregates by province and urban/rural, with quantities, expenditure and the sample behind each.
downloads.title: Household fuel use

downloads.coverage: Ten fiscal years · HDIP · OGRA · NFDC
downloads.dek: Coal and gas by published customer group, and the gas a fertiliser plant turns into ammonia kept apart from the gas it burns.

downloads.dek: Clinker and cement as each company reported it, with national output controls and clinker trade. Company figures are never split across plants.
downloads.title: Industrial production

downloads.dek: National and provincial output, and the gas each field supplies to each utility system.
downloads.title: Gas and oil production

downloads.dek: Utility sales, pipeline lengths and customer counts. Unaccounted-for gas is here too — and it is not a leakage measurement.

downloads.dek: How households say their waste is collected, and JMP's sanitation shares. Reported services, not measured tonnage.

downloads.dek: Generation, collection, open burning and the unresolved remainder. An estimate from a per-capita rate and a fate partition — not measured municipal tonnage.
downloads.title: Waste flows (modelled)

downloads.dek: Pakistan Railways' own metered diesel and furnace oil, with train-, passenger- and tonne-kilometres beside it.
downloads.title: Railway fuel and traffic

downloads.dek: Aircraft movements, passengers, cargo and mail by airport across eighteen fiscal years, and the same year cut by airline.
downloads.title: Airport movements and passengers

downloads.dek: The twenty technical fields behind every activity row — source file, row, column, transformation and combinability — joined to the tables above on Record ID.
downloads.title: Source details for the activity tables

downloads.dek: What every column of every activity table means, one line per column.
downloads.title: Column guide for the activity tables

downloads.dek: Cumulative registered stock as at 30 June, by district and class. Not observed traffic, and not an active fleet.
downloads.title: Registered vehicles by district

parquet.note: all-string Parquet written from the CSV text; the CSV is the identity

aggregation.closure: ⚠ UNACCOUNTED-FOR GAS IS NOT AN EMISSION FIGURE AND MUST NEVER BE USED AS ONE. It is the difference between gas purchased and gas billed - theft, meter error and billing differences alongside physical leakage - and multiplying it by a GWP is the error this contract exists to prevent. The three flow rows are not additive: marketable gas already contains the other two

parquet.note: all-string Parquet written from the CSV text; the CSV is the identity

parquet.note: all-string Parquet written from the CSV text; the CSV is the identity

parquet.note: all-string Parquet written from the CSV text; the CSV is the identity

known_limitations.message: the ten-fiscal-year panel covers the ESTIMATED sources alone (coverage_scope=covered_sources_only): grid power is inside it only for the species its admission register prices (oil and diesel SO2) and otherwise ships beside it as a controlled-to-uncontrolled screening pair; industrial combustion (rc58), IPPU process pollutants and fugitive NMVOC with flaring (rc59) are inside it as provisional estimates from the source-class register, with what each register cannot price typed absent per species in pakemis_air_coverage_matrix.csv - this is not a complete national seven-species inventory and does not claim to be, so 'the largest source' means the largest of the sources estimated here. Agricultural management/grazing NOx includes the adopted chemical partition of volatilised nitrogen; that partition is held in conditional intervals and tested separately by a nitrogen-conserving attribution diagnostic, not measured in Pakistan

the integrated air-pollutant layer reports native kt of the named species, never CO2e, with assurance that is uneven across sectors (pakemis_air_coverage_matrix.csv states each sector, species and period) and outside every greenhouse-gas total

grid power is covered only for the species its admission register prices (oil and diesel SO2); for every other species it has no covered estimate and a screening scenario pair ships beside the panel. Within the register modules the classes no admissible factor or series can price - urea finishing, nitric acid, lime, glass, venting, post-meter NMVOC, LNG terminals, captive solids, bagasse - are recorded NE with their activity beside them, never counted as zero
known_limitations.scope: query_air, sectors power and the register modules' typed classes

known_limitations.message: the particulate strata contain one another (BC and OC inside PM2.5, PM2.5 inside PM10, PM10 inside TSP), so a sum across pollutants is refused, never computed

every sector's air layer is placed with its own streams' geography, for all ten fiscal periods (fact_air_adm1_year, fact_air_adm2_year). What a grain does not place stays typed, never zeroed, in pakemis_air_unallocated_by_year.csv - aviation cruise below the provinces, and mass outside the district frame - and a request for a sector the provincial or district table does not hold is refused naming the sectors it does
the 1990-2024 calendar-year air series is national and agriculture-only; provinces and districts carry the ten fiscal periods (FY2015-16..FY2024-25), not calendar years
calendar-year values exist only for the agriculture reconstruction (fact_annual_calendar); every other sector is fiscal (July-June) and a calendar request is refused, never computed

every period is published on one fixed district frame (geoBoundaries-gbOpen-PAK-ADM2-2019, 152 canonical units); eleven units were carved out of larger districts during the window, so an earlier year's row for such a district is the mass that would fall inside TODAY's boundary, not a figure any administration reported at the time. The contemporaneous geography is not held - see abs-adm2-frame-vintage

the ADM2 products carry native gas mass at module grain; AR6 CO2e is available nationally and at ADM1 in the monthly table fact_adm1_month. The annual ADM1 table fact_adm1_year and every ADM2 table carry AR5 only

S_TAN is the reference. L_TAN, S_IPCC and L_IPCC alter household dung destination and nitrogen methods. All four are annual and monthly native-gas calculations, not additive components or probability-weighted scenarios.

Covered industrial-combustion emissions fell, reflecting lower recorded fuel use. This does not mean Pakistan's total industrial emissions declined; several industrial sources are reported elsewhere or remain outside the inventory. The industry (1.A.2) series is a REPORTED-FUEL estimate: its two largest streams, brick-kiln coal and cement-sector coal, are the official HDIP coal-by-consumer allocation (Finance Division Statistical Supplement Table 14.1(4), marked '** Estimated'), which swings threefold across the window and falls sharply after FY2020-21. The published coal account compares production, imports and station consumption and retains unresolved quantities. Its allocation changes must not be read as verified reductions from mitigation or efficiency. The column the Supplement prints as 'Cement' is the primary publication's 'Cement/Other Industry', so other industrial coal may sit inside it unsplit. Dated fleet and fuel-use alternatives are separate structural cases, without assigned probabilities

reporting_sector files each stream where IPCC 2006 reports it, in the module vocabulary, beside sector_id (the module that computed it): captive gas self-generation (1.A.2, computed by the power module because it shares the plant register and factor table) reports under industry; railways' unresolved '1.A.2/1.A.4.c' and transport's mixed off-road (1.A.4.c/1.A.2) keep their modules until their splits are published. The axis is additive with sector_id at every grain - the same atoms regrouped, no mass moved - and is declared per stream in data/stream_reporting_sector.csv (pkinv.core.declared.match_prefix, a stream with no row raises). It is answerable at every grain: the district tables carry the column too (since rc54 the cube keys its accumulator on the module and reporting sector together), so the industry reporting sector at district grain includes the captive generation the axis exists to include. The air lane stays module-keyed

the economic-sector view regroups the same atoms by what the activity is: 'industrial' = the industry and ippu REPORTING sectors - 1.A.2 manufacturing combustion including the captive generation the power module computes (through the reporting_sector axis) plus every 2.x process category; every other sector keeps its module. It is additive with the IPCC view. Its industrial aggregate is 'covered direct industrial sources' - the priced boundary only. Since rc52 that boundary holds ammonia (2.B.1), iron and steel (2.C.1) and lubricant use (2.D.1) as ten-year series beside cement; nitric acid (a pair), HFCs and SF6, lime, glass, soda ash (NA in IPPU) and industrial wastewater are screened or absent and are NOT inside it; each enters only with an explicitly supported period and boundary. The common core covers FY2015-16 through FY2024-25; partial FY2025-26 records cannot be summed into it
grid cells stay in the NetCDF products (CF-1.8), which the release manifest lists and hashes; the API reads a cell from the file and the map tiles are visual only
the residual territories row and the census units the boundary file does not draw carry mass at ADM1 and are named rows without geometry
no land-use, land-use-change or forestry flux enters any total; an exploratory Tier-1 module publishes a provisional sink outside every total
Set 0 at Tier 1; requires land-use/management-change activity data.
known_limitations.scope: 3.C.4 Managed soils - N from SOC mineralisation (FSOM)

known_limitations.message: Not estimated: assumed negligible on Pakistan's alkaline/calcareous cropland soils, pending national lime-use activity data (NE rather than NO, since the activity is not demonstrated to be absent). rc39 A4: this NE used to share an engine category with 3.H, which published a 0.000000 Gg liming row - a zero asserts a measurement, so the row was withdrawn and 3.G now maps to no engine category at all. Eq 11.12 and the IPCC Table 11.2 factors are held; only the activity statistic is missing.
Minor; not separately quantified. No IPCC 2006 category exists for it.

MATERIAL AND SCREENED, previously undeclared: OGRA's held commercial gas class (45 MMCFD, counted once as post-meter leakage and never as combustion) and the chart-read commercial LPG (~520 kt) screen at roughly 2.4 Mt CO2e between them (outputs/commercial_institutional_audit_2024.csv), below Pakistan's own BUR-1 commercial filing of 3.8 Mt as a two-stream floor should be. Stays NE for stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the commercial share of retail petroleum is unresolvable within OCAC's held classes without the HDIP commercial energy balance. See commercial-institutional.

Domestic biogas digesters exist in Pakistan (PCRET-supported units, cattle-belt provinces); the programme installation records that would count them have not been obtained here, and HIES carries no biogas consumption item to fall back on. Combustion CO2 would be biogenic; the reportable quantities are digester leakage CH4 and the manure-management transfer, both unestimated. Believed small: electrification and gas/LPG penetration cap the niche. See residential-biogas.

The 8.3 kt of charcoal burned implies roughly 35-50 kt of wood carbonised upstream (4-6 kg wood per kg charcoal), with kiln CH4 that IPCC books to the producing category. No Pakistani charcoal-production statistic exists; the quantity is bounded by the burned charcoal itself and is far below the firewood stream's uncertainty band.
Tier 1 wants refinery throughput and well counts; the Year Book carries production only. Small against production.
known_limitations.scope: 1.B.2 Fugitive emissions - refining, well drilling, testing and servicing

known_limitations.message: The largest omission inside 1.B.2 and the cheapest to close: IPCC drives it from utility sales, and OGRA publishes an unaccounted-for-gas line in a free report this inventory already uses for three other numbers.
known_limitations.scope: 1.B.2 Fugitive emissions - gas transmission and distribution

known_limitations.message: Coal mining and handling. PARTIALLY SCREENED: the dominant share of production was held all along - NEPRA Table 21 mine-mouth deliveries to the four Thar plants, 13.24 Mt lignite in FY2023-24 - and the Tier 1 surface band on it is 0.07-0.55 Mt CO2e (outputs/fugitives_coal_screen_2024.csv). The bound is partial by construction and stays NE: underground mining (Balochistan, KP, Punjab) runs thirty times the surface low per tonne, no underground production figure is held, and no Pakistani mine-gas measurement exists. See fugitive-solid-fuels and coal-mine-gas.

The estimated category is municipal solid waste only. Industrial solid waste reaching disposal sites has no national tonnage here; the provincial EPAs' industrial waste returns are the closing source. See waste-industrial.

Construction and demolition waste is largely inert (near-zero degradable carbon), so its CH4 potential is small by composition - but its tonnage is unquantified and it is a distinct absence from industrial waste, with a different closing source: the Urban Unit's tehsil-level service and facility mapping covers Punjab and has not been obtained. See waste-construction.

Municipal composting operates at city scale - Lahore's composting facility is the largest, with smaller plants elsewhere - but no national throughput series has been compiled here. Believed small against 4.A, and the omission biases 4.A UP rather than the total down: the streams composting diverts currently sit inside the collected tonnage and decay at the disposal MCF, so estimating 4.B would move emissions out of 4.A, not add them. See waste-biological-treatment.
known_limitations.scope: 4.B Biological treatment of solid waste (composting, anaerobic digestion)

known_limitations.message: No municipal-scale incineration operates in Pakistan, but hospital and clinical-waste incinerators do; their throughput has not been obtained here, so no magnitude is stated. See waste-incineration.
Needs industrial output by sector and the organic load of each sector's wastewater; neither is held.

The non-gas captive fleet, now sized from the register itself: of the 1,105 plants, the fuel-labelled capacity is 769 MW furnace oil (64 plants), 366 MW bagasse (25), 351 MW coal (9), 126 MW biomass (9) and 64 MW diesel (3), against 1,294 MW of gas - so the unestimated fleet is comparable in capacity to the estimated one. What has not been obtained is metered fuel for any of it; the estimated category is natural gas only and its name says so. See captive-nongas-fuels.
known_limitations.scope: 1.A.2 Captive self-generation - furnace oil / diesel / coal / bagasse

known_limitations.message: NO LONGER THE GAP IT WAS: the rc46 activation put the measured HDIP coal-by-consumer series INTO the reference - brick-kiln coal 2.78 and cement-sector coal 10.80 Mt through the industrial_solid_fuels_1a2 scope gate - and the supply-consumption identity (imports+production exhausts the consumer columns to ~0.5 kt in 8 of 9 years) closed the old industrial-coal/petcoke refusal: 'other industrial coal' is definitionally ~zero and petcoke rides the Comtrade lane. EDGAR puts Pakistani industrial combustion near 44 Mt CO2e against the engine's 22.58, and the ~15.9 Mt benchmark residual (outputs/industry_fuel_ledger_2024.csv) is now benchmark disagreement over an exhaustive consumer series, bounded but not decomposable: its remaining named claimants are the cement transferred-intensity model's EXCESS over the measured series (+1.2 to +4.9 Mt, configuration cement_kiln_fuel_in_scope) and the process-bagasse ceiling (0.39 Mt). The brick and captive screenings retired at rc47 Wave 0 - superseded_by_reference_stream in the fuel ledger; adding either to a reference that books the measured series would double-count, which is exactly what their configurations briefly did. What would still move this category is a Pakistani kiln heat-intensity audit (to settle the cement excess) and industrial fuel by type beyond the Statistical Supplement's consumer split - HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook (paid, eyb@hdip.gov.pk) or OCAC (members-only).
known_limitations.scope: 1.A.2 Manufacturing industries and construction - all other

known_limitations.message: The fuel is IDENTIFIED AND PRICED, the scope is not attributed: the OCAC customer bridge assigns 120,758 t of military/government jet fuel, 4,542 t of 100LL and 12,282 t of unresolved government JP-1 - about 0.435 Mt CO2, priced as memo rows in outputs/aviation_totals_fy2023_24.csv, restated as the observed-unallocated account outputs/aviation_unallocated_fuel_fy2023_24.csv (each tonne with an evidence class, a disposition and a named closer), and as three independent national configurations (military_government_in_scope, general_aviation_in_scope, unresolved_jp1_in_scope; the split of one lumped axis) - but no record attributes the activity between military operations and civil government use, and IPCC reports military aviation under 1A5b. See aviation-1a5b-scope.

Refrigerant leakage from vehicle air-conditioning is IPPU 2.F.1, not combustion, so it is outside the fuel anchor by construction - but it is a real transport-fleet emission this inventory does not yet report anywhere: the 2.F species-aware bank engine is implemented and the Ozone Secretariat's 2024 consumption control is loaded, but the mobile-air-conditioning application split has not been reconciled here. See transport-mobile-ac-hfc.

SCREENED, not estimated: the two blockers the earlier row named - a marine factor choice and a domestic/foreign boundary review - are made in sectors/transport/navigation_screen.py, and every held OCAC edition's Domestic Bunkers row is converted in outputs/transport_navigation_screen_2024.csv (3,054 t HSD in the FY2023-24 reference year, 0.0098 Mt CO2e on IPCC Tables 3.5.2/3.5.3). It stays NE for two stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the ten held editions span 32 to 8,342 t with no trend - an activity that volatile needs the port-side series before it can carry an E. See marine-domestic.

Would be a memo item if it were estimated. NOT to be taken from the 'Overseas/Export' line of OGRA Table 2.1: that line is exported furnace-oil CARGO, not fuel bunkered at Pakistani ports - 1.01 Mt for FY2023-24 against 1.11 Mt of furnace-oil exports reported for calendar 2024. The one figure that does exist is Pakistan's own: BTR1 books 1.A.3.d.i international marine bunkers at 0.0393 Mt CO2, 0.040 Mt CO2e, for 2020-21 (sources/UNFCCC/btr1_2024.txt line 843) - two orders of magnitude below the roughly 3 Mt the OGRA line would give, which is why the trap matters. An earlier version of this row said Pakistan had no formal bunkering market until 2026 and let that carry the absence; a market's absence is not the absence of fuel delivered, and the national submission books some. Recorded so nobody builds the sector on that line, and so nobody reads this as nothing to estimate.

The EEDB publishes HC (unspeciated exhaust hydrocarbons); the vocabulary rule forbids renaming it NMVOC without a documented methane basis, so the nine-year panel writes aviation NMVOC as NE while the HC series ships as a supplemental species. See air-aviation-nmvoc.

Needs control-device inventory and performance by unit: which plants have precipitators or flue-gas desulphurisation and at what removal efficiency. The five NEPRA Licensees HSE Performance Evaluation Reports were fetched and audited in August 2026: they publish no per-plant equipment or emissions, but their questionnaire scores licensees on air-quality controls and on submitting environmental monitoring reports - so the data exists at NEPRA as unpublished licensee submissions, and the route is a request to its HSE department. Applying a removal rate without it would be inventing the number that matters most, since it spans an order of magnitude between uncontrolled and well-controlled.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - power generation, as actually emitted

known_limitations.message: EMEP/EEA 2023 lists NH3 as not estimated for gas, liquid and solid fuel combustion in 1.A.2 and AP-42's combustion chapters carry no NH3 row; the one South Asian kiln measurement (Stockwell et al. 2016: below detection for a zig-zag kiln, 0.429 g/kg fuel for a clamp kiln) is not held. Absent, not zero. See air-industry-nh3.

HDIP labels the column Cement/Other Industry; the clinker-implied kiln-coal band leaves 1.4-6.4 Mt of it outside the kilns in most years, users unidentified, so no equipment or control can be assigned. The tonnage is written in the industry air detail file beside a typed absence. See air-industry-coal-users.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - other-industry coal inside HDIP's cement column

known_limitations.message: The captive register sizes coal-fired captive plants by capacity only and no metered tonne is held; the greenhouse-gas screening prices a bracket outside every total and the air layer types the class absent. See air-industry-captive-solid.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - captive self-generation on coal

known_limitations.message: No mill-level bagasse fuel series is held (the all-cane ceiling is a greenhouse-gas configuration, not an activity); grid-connected bagasse cogeneration stays in the power screening. See air-industry-bagasse.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - industrial bagasse process heat

known_limitations.message: The EMEP 2.B.10.a row is a sector-wide E-PRTR/Eurostat ratio, inadmissible for a prilling tower (it would print 330 kt of TSP from 6.6 Mt of urea); AP-42 8.2 is the applicable chapter and every epa.gov address tried returned 403. The urea tonnage is written beside the typed absence. See air-ippu-urea.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - urea prilling and granulation particulate and ammonia

known_limitations.message: The EMEP 2.B.2 factor is held; no fiscal nitric-acid production series is (one calendar-2022 point, which cannot back-cast to FY2015-16). See air-ippu-nitric.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - nitric acid process NOx

known_limitations.message: The EMEP 2.A.2 chapter is held; no lime production series is (PBS QIM lists no lime item; lime CO2 is NE in the greenhouse-gas panel for the same reason). See air-ippu-lime.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - lime kiln process particulate

known_limitations.message: The EMEP 2.A.3 chapter is held; the QIM glass item is an area (square metres of sheet) that cannot be priced per tonne without a conversion nobody publishes. See air-ippu-glass.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - glass furnace process particulate

known_limitations.message: EMEP/EEA 2023 2.B.1 lists NMVOC, SOx and PM2.5 as not estimated for ammonia production and 2.B.7 lists PM10, PM2.5 and BC as not estimated for soda ash; each is a typed absence row inside the class detail, never a zero. See air-ippu-species.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - ammonia and soda ash process species not estimated by the chapters

known_limitations.message: The fugitives module carries venting inside its production CH4 factors and holds no vented-volume series; EMEP 1.B.2.c Tier 1 prices flaring only. See air-fugitives-venting.

The module's post-meter CH4 carries the leak; an NMVOC term needs the C2+ content of sales gas, which is not held (gas_ch4_fraction 0.90 is CH4 by mass, not an NMVOC fraction). See air-fugitives-composition.

The EMEP 1.B.2 chapters print no Tier 1 NMVOC factor for regasification terminals; the imported-oil transport factor is held but the module's oil-pipeline anchor is a diagnostic length, not a throughput. See air-fugitives-segments.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - LNG import terminal and oil pipeline NMVOC

known_limitations.message: EMEP/EEA 2023 1.B.2.c lists NH3 not estimated for flaring; 1.B.2.a.iv lists BC not estimated for refining. Typed absence rows inside the class detail; the fugitives NH3 cell of the coverage matrix is NE on this row. See air-fugitives-species.
known_limitations.scope: (air) Air pollutants - flare and refinery species not estimated by the chapters

known_limitations.message: The 2022 CRT contains lime activity and emissions, but an independent FY2023-24 marketed-plus-captive lime series by type has not been compiled here. See lime-production.

One of two identified plants has production (Fatima Sadiqabad, 563,701 t, calendar 2022) and its ACM0019 abatement history is loaded; the Wave 4 screening prices the unabated and last-verified-abatement readings as configurations, and the category stays NE until matched-year production and operating abatement evidence arrive. This row was MISSING from the register until Wave 4 - the same silent-absence class the 1.A.4.a audit closed - while the sector-level IPPU view carried it at critical materiality. See nitric-acid-production.

The Ozone Secretariat reports a 2024 HFC-consumption control and the species-aware equipment-bank engine is implemented. Chemical/application imports, installed banks, leakage, retirement and recovery are not yet reconciled, so consumption is not treated as annual emissions.
